coverage.main: Read all eleven pages of arXiv 1911.02466v2 (Sections 1-6, Algorithm 1, Tables 1-3, Figures 1-5, references, appendix Tables 4-5) and the ten-page CVPR 2020 open-access version; Section 5.4 and Table 3 print identical text and values in both.
coverage.supplement: The appendix (Tables 4-5: lambda initialisations and untargeted white-box results) is embedded in arXiv v2 and read. It adds no transfer result.
coverage.excluded_results: Tables 1, 2 and 5 are white-box success rates and perturbation sizes on Inception v3; Figure 4 is robustness of white-box examples to JPEG/bit-depth reduction on the source; Figures 1, 3 and 5 are qualitative. Footnote 2 states Table 3 differs from an earlier arXiv version; only v2/CVPR values are used.

result_groups.population: Subset of the 1,000 ImageNet-compatible development images that all four models (Inception v3 source; GoogLeNet, VGG-16, ResNet-152 targets) originally classify correctly: 767 images. Untargeted I-FGSM, C&W, DDN, PerC-C&W and PerC-AL examples at kappa = 20 and 40
result_groups.outcome: transfer success rate: an example 'is regarded to be transferable to a new model if it can also induce misclassification of that model'
result_groups.evidence: The paper explicitly restricts evaluation to images every model classifies correctly (clean-correct for each target). The word 'also' presupposes source success, but no explicit rule removes source failures; white-box kappa = 40 success is below 100% for I-FGSM (99.9%) and DDN (98.1%) on the 1,000 images (Table 2).

f1.evidence: Clean correctness is used as a filter (767 of 1,000 jointly correct), but no per-model clean accuracy is printed.

f2.evidence: 'We report results on a subset of our data containing images that all four models originally classify correctly' (767 images). Positive conditioning evidence.

f3.evidence: No explicit source-success filter or inclusion statement; source success is not 100% for every method at kappa = 40.

f4.evidence: With the stated 767 denominator, 27 of 30 one-decimal cells map to a unique count (survey/count_reconstruction.py), but the three 2.4% cells admit no integer numerator (18/767 = 2.35%, 19/767 = 2.48%). Counts are therefore not reconstructed for the table.

f5.evidence: All compared attacks are minimum-perturbation or confidence-margin methods (I-FGSM repeated with increasing bound, C&W, DDN, PerC) run until a kappa margin is met; Table 1 reports measured L2/L-infinity sizes, which are not a budget. This is an explicit design choice, not missing reporting.

f6.evidence: The official repository releases the 1,000 images, attack code and a notebook whose transferability cell uses public torchvision targets. As pinned, that cell selects images on which the four models' predictions agree (not ground-truth correctness), scores against the source's clean prediction, and passes the clean tensor to VGG-16 and ResNet-152. Adversarial images are not released. Which code version produced Table 3 is not established; not executed.

artifact_checks.result: Linked in the paper. Listed via the GitHub API (1,016 files, head 1 February 2023): dataset/images (1,000 PNGs) and images.csv, perc_al.py, perc_cw.py, differential_color_functions.py, main.ipynb. Notebook cell 5 ('Evaluation on transferability') was read: eligibility mask = pairwise agreement of the four models' clean predictions; success = prediction differs from Inception v3's clean prediction; the VGG-16 and ResNet-152 lines evaluate X_ori; denominator = all eligible images; no stored outputs. Not executed.

bounds_checks.reason: Rates are conditional on joint clean correctness, so max(0, rate - clean error) is not the matched unconditional bound; no unconditional attacked error is reported.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. The notebook observations describe the released code as pinned, not the configuration that produced Table 3.
